transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Gomez (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Atlas ML), Priya Kapoor (Atlas SRE), Liam O'Connor (Atlas DS)

Summary: quick review of quantization experiment results (INT8 and FP8), quality-impact discussion, perf deltas on 2x A100 dedicated pool, tuning suggestions and next steps for canary. Some transcription noise and mis-heard acronyms present.

Topics: results overview; quality regressions; throughput/latency numbers; batching & cache tuning; canary plan; compliance questions.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick check-in for week three of the quantization POC. Elena and I will run through the latest numbers, Rajiv and team you sent the evaluation set so we have some real traffic replicas, thanks for that.
[00:18] Rajiv: yeah thanks, and good morning. we got the eval back, a lot of thanks to Elena who set up the pipeline, so excited to see the deltas.
[00:25] Elena: cool, i'll share my screen after Samir's overview, i'll show the perf spreadsheet and the sample outputs. quick note, some of the F-P eight rows are labeled FP-8 and sometimes F-P8 in the csv, so, uh, small naming mess.
[00:40] Samir: ha, standard. quick bullets: baseline is FP16 model pinned to v1.2 (no pruning). we ran two quant configs on the dedicated pool (2x A100, 40GB): INT8 symmetric quant with activation calibration on 2k samples; and FP8 (narrow dynamic range) with the compiler-optimized kernels.
[00:58] Samir: key headline: INT8 gives roughly 1.7x throughput vs FP16 at batch=8, and reduces GPU memory by ~40%. FP8 is close to FP16 for latency but has slightly better memory and a 1.2x throughput bump in some runs. Quality: FP8 is almost indistinguishable from FP16 on our metrics, INT8 shows small regressions on long-context summarization prompts.
[01:24] Liam: can you quantify "small regressions"? like rouge/bleu or hallucination rate?
[01:30] Elena: yeah we ran the 5k dev subset — precision/recall for the entity extraction probes dropped ~2.4% absolute on INT8; Rouge-L for long summaries dropped ~3.1 points on INT8, FP8 was within 0.5 pts. hallucination audits show about a 1.5x increase in spurious factual errors for INT8 on >1k token contexts.
[01:56] Rajiv: hmm ok that's the area of concern, our workload has a lot of long docs, average seq length is around 800 tokens and a heavy tail to 3k.
[02:06] Priya: and remember we need stable p95 latency under 500ms for SNOW endpoint, what's our p95 numbers?
[02:13] Elena: p95 numbers, baseline FP16 at batch=8 was ~420ms p95 per request. INT8 p95 improved to ~360ms (so about 14% lower), FP8 averaged ~400ms. Throughput (tokens/sec) at batch=8: FP16 ~12k tok/s, INT8 ~20k tok/s, FP8 ~14.5k tok/s (these are aggregate from the A100 pool).
[02:40] Rajiv: interesting INT8 wins perf but has quality regressions on long sequences. is that due to KV cache quantization or attention kernel precision?
[02:48] Elena: mostly activations and layernorm sensitivity in the long-attention blocks, the KV cache appears fine but we saw small drift in softmax numerics when mixed with INT8 matmuls. compiler team flagged a path where we can keep KV cache in FP16 while doing matmuls in INT8 — tradeoff will cut memory benefits but stabilize long-context quality.
[03:10] Samir: yeah that hybrid approach is promising: INT8 compute for feedforward/matmul, keep attention/KV in FP16. gives ~1.4x throughput still but drops the quality delta to under 1% on our metrics.
[03:23] Liam: can we run a quick A/B with hybrid vs full-INT8 on the 1k-long tail?
[03:29] Elena: yes, we can queue that. that's part of the 10k eval we'll run.
[03:33] Priya: operationally, if we move to hybrid we need the deployment config and a fallback policy — if model accuracy regresses beyond threshold we auto-fallback to FP16 instance pool. who owns the rollback?
[03:44] Samir: Redwood can set the rollout policy; we suggest canary at 5% traffic for 24 hours on dedicated pool and auto-rollback if QoR drop >2% on monitored eval prompts. we'll send a config template.
[03:57] Rajiv: good. pricing/credits question: INT8 reduces GPU-hours thanks to memory, do you have updated cost estimates?
[04:04] Samir: preliminary cost delta: INT8 reduces inference cost about 28–35% for this workload on dedicated A100, hybrid about 15–20% savings, FP8 around 10–12% vs FP16. exact numbers in spreadsheet.
[04:18] Liam: curious if batch size tuning could reduce INT8 quality issues? larger batch == more stable numerics?
[04:24] Elena: batching mostly affects throughput and latency; numerics are per-token. but we do see slightly less variance at higher batch sizes because of kernel selection smoothing; still long-context errors persist.
[04:36] Samir: operational notes: we used Redwood Optimize to suggest batch=8 and kv-cache TTL of 30s for interactive workloads; for Atlas's profile (avg seq 800) we recommended batch 6-10. we can attach the Optimize recommendations.
[04:50] Priya: security/compliance: are we logging raw prompts for evaluation? we have to be careful — SOC2 scope restricts PII retention.
[04:58] Samir: agreed. current eval logs are redacted; we only store examples with PII masked. Redwood's Private deployment can keep logs in your VPC; or we can provide a masked sample export for quality checks.
[05:12] Rajiv: ok please send the redaction script and the sample export.
[05:15] Elena: noted. i'll include the script link in the follow-up.
[05:19] [crosstalk] Liam: also can we get regression examples where FP16 wins vs INT8 — we want concrete prompts to review with product.
[05:26] Elena: yes, we'll attach top 50 failure cases and categorize by error type.
[05:30] Samir: timeline / next steps — we propose: 1) Elena runs hybrid INT8/FP16 KV eval + 10k quality run; 2) Samir sends perf sheet + canary rollout template; 3) Atlas provides traffic histogram and compliance scope; 4) schedule canary for next Tuesday on dedicated pool. does that sound right?
[05:48] Rajiv: yes, + also include cost/runbook for auto-rollback, we need an SRE sign-off.
[05:54] Priya: i will review once we have the canary playbook.
[05:57] Samir: perfect. quick Q from Liam — any vendor/competitor constraints we should know? Rajiv mentioned possible internal preference for NVIDIA's Triton infra but you were open to Redwood runtime?
[06:07] Rajiv: we evaluated Triton but it's extra ops work; Redwood's managed kernels were appealing if we can match quality.
[06:13] Elena: on the kernel side we do use vendor-supplied cuBLAS/cuDNN paths for FP16/FP8 and our compiler chooses optimized matmul kernels for INT8. sometimes vendor kernels have slightly different numerics which explains small diffs.
[06:28] Liam: any examples of weird transcriptions in logs? (laughter)
[06:31] Samir: we will try to avoid that — but transcript: Speaker labels may be fuzzy.
[06:36] Rajiv: last thing, can you include the bench commands and docker image tags used? we need exact reproducibility.
[06:42] Elena: yes bench commands, config and docker tag are in the spreadsheet — image: redwood/runtime:v2.14-quant-aug1 (note: some runs used v2.13 -> included in notes).
[06:53] Samir: ok wrap up — we'll send the perf spreadsheet, failure cases, redaction script, and the proposed canary rollout template by EOD tomorrow. action items recorded.
[07:02] Priya: thanks everyone, will look out for docs and will try to get the traffic histogram by Thursday.
[07:08] Rajiv: thanks team.

End of transcript.
